title.narrative: Togo Essential Quality Health Services For Universal Health Coverage Project

description.narrative: The proposed Additional Financing (AF) will add to the existing operation, with revisions planned to broaden the range of activities and address identified challenges to help the project achieve its development objective. This AF will provide US$70 million (IDA credit) and a US$1 million grant to expand the Togo Essential Quality Health Services for Universal Health Coverage Project. The AF addresses funding gaps, cost overruns, and supports new activities to improve health service delivery, digitalization, and emergency preparedness. This AF aims to expand the scope of the parent project to address critical gaps in the supply and demand of quality health and nutrition services, particularly as partner resources in Togo are declining. The operation will also address cost overruns due to inflation, underestimated construction and renovation costs, and the economic impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic. A Level II restructuring of the project is also planned, which will include: (i) the addition of new activities under Components 1 and 3; (ii) revisions to the results framework to more accurately capture implementation progress and reflect the expanded scope; (iii) revisions to the implementation arrangements with the adoption of a new constitution in March 2024; and (iv) an extension of the project's closing date by 22 months, to February 29, 2028, to allow adequate time for the completion of planned activities. All revisions are consistent with the World Bank's Country Partnership Framework (CPF) for Togo for FY25-FY29 (Report No. 185419-TG), which was approved in May 2024, where this proposed AF is aligned with High Level Outcome 2 (HLO2, Improving Human Capital) that will support Togo's progress towards UHC by improving access to health facilities, increasing human resources in the health sector, and foster a higher coverage of the NSHI Scheme. The Project Cost after Additional Financing will be US$141 million equivalent (including parent project, restructuring, AF, and trust fund).Project progress. Since its approval in March 2021 and effectiveness in August 2021, US$50.44 million (77% of parent project funds) have been disbursed as of October 2025, with the remainder amount fully committed. The project surpassed two out of four PDO indicators and met or exceeded five out of 14 intermediate results indicators; has delivered over 15 million essential health service visits, exceeding its targets; deployed 1,815 health professionals; constructed or renovated 122 health facilities; launched the National Social Health Insurance Scheme, which now covers 4.4 million people; and has seen accelerated implementation across all major components, with further progress anticipated as Performance-Based Conditions are validated and construction and renovation efforts continue.Proposed New Activities. Component 1: Increasing the demand for and supply of quality health and nutrition services (Original: US$32.60m; Revised during Restructuring #1: US$18.82m; AF: US$2.78m; AF HEPR TF: US$1.00m; New Total: US$22.60m). This component will continue to provide support to improving and increasing the supply and demand of quality health and nutrition services with a focus on access, enrolment of poor/vulnerable populations under the NSHI Scheme, equitable distribution of human resources, and tracer drug availability. The AF will help to reinforce the activities under Sub-component 1.1: Increasing access to essential health and nutrition services to support programs that are managed at the central level by the MoHPH to increase immunization coverage and improve RMNCAH+N outcomes. Additional funds will also be allocated to Sub-component 1.4: Increasing tracer drug availability at PHU facilities to better support supply chain management and purchasing of essential RMNCAH+N commodities such as family planning, and medications/products/materials for antenatal care, postnatal care, management of infections and diseases. A new sub-component will be added, Sub-component 1.5: Strengthening Health Emergency Preparedness and Response (AF HEPR TF: US$1.00m), which will strengthen efficiency and responsiveness to health security and emergencies. The AF will finance disease surveillance and response through (i) laboratory infrastructure, material and equipment for epidemic-prone diseases, (ii) training; (iii) strengthening the disease alert management system; (iv) epidemic communication activities; and (vii) ensuring uninterrupted access to essential medications, particularly for immunocompromised populations. Component 2: Bringing health facilities and services close to households (Original: US$30.00m; Revised during Restructuring #1: US$43.78m; AF: US$37.92m; New Total: US$81.70m). This component will continue to support improvements to access quality healthcare through newly constructed or renovated climate-resilient PHC facilities in disadvantaged areas as well as equipping these facilities with the necessary medical equipment and supplies, ensuring they are fully operational and capable of delivering the required services. Under Subcomponent 2.1: Increasing access of vulnerable populations to health facilities and services, the AF will enable the completion of the construction of 80 new health facilities and the renovation of 90 health facilities. Under Sub-component 2.2: Providing equipment to the newly built health facilities, one critical aspect that will also be supported is related to asset management and maintenance such as equipment purchased under the project. As part as the Level II restructuring, a cost-effective digital asset management system pilot will be implemented to replace manual record-keeping, thereby improving the tracking, monitoring, and maintenance of medical equipment in Togo. A real-time register of medical equipment will be established across national public health facilities, enable remote verification of equipment presence, improve maintenance management, and track asset depreciation and valuation over time.Component 3: Strengthening the National Social Health Insurance Scheme (Original: US$4.30m; AF:US$26.09m; New Total: US$30.39m). This component will continue to support the Government to operationalize the NSHI Scheme to ensure better financial protection for the population, particularly the poor and vulnerable, as well as to ensure comprehensive communication and to build awareness of the NSHI Scheme through communication and community engagement. The AF will specifically support Sub-component 3.1: Establishing and supporting the operations of the agencies managing the NSHI Scheme through the enhancement of digital infrastructure in health facilities and at the NSHI management bodies, crucial for improving the efficiency and effectiveness of health care delivery through the inclusion of PBCs. PBC2 for the enrollment of poor and vulnerable groups is available to finance these activities. The new PBCs to be financed are related to: (i) availability of EHRs in health facilities contracted under the NSHI Scheme; (ii) interoperability of the information systems of the NSHI Scheme's management bodies (INAM, CNSS); and (iii) health facilities that utilize a digitized process for NSHI Scheme claims. These new PBCs will also enable the creation of new jobs, particularly for young graduates and technicians to modernize the health sector. The AF will support the management bodies to have the necessary digital tools to manage the NSHI Scheme effectively. This includes ensuring the digitalization of the reimbursement process, ensuring that healthcare services provided by health facilities are reimbursed in real-time, enhancing transparency and accountability, ensuring that funds are promptly allocated and disbursed, thus improving the financial flows within the NSHI Scheme. condition.narrative: Schedule 2-I. A.1.(a). No later than six (6) months after the Project Effective Date, the Recipient shall establish within theOffice of the President, and thereafter maintain, throughout Project implementation, a project coordination unit with terms ofreference, composition and resources acceptable to the Association (“Project Coordination Unit” or “PCU”).

Schedule 2-I. B.1. No later than six (6) months after the Effective Date, the Recipient shall adopt and thereafter implement theProject in accordance with the project implementation manual (“Project Implementation Manual” or “PIM”), with terms and conditionssatisfactory to the Association.

Schedule 2-I. C.3. For purposes of the implementation Parts 1.1, 1.2 and 1.4, the Recipient, through the Ministry of Health, PublicHygiene and Universal Access to Care, shall enter into an agreement (“Subsidiary Agreement”) with the Togo Social Health InsuranceAgency (“TSHIA”), in form and substance acceptable to the Association.

Schedule 2-I. D.(b).(i). For purposes of counter verification of the payments under the Eligible Expenditures for the PBCs underPart 1.1, 1.2 and 1.4 of the Project, the TSHIA shall:(i) No later than twelve (12) months after the Effective Date, and with theapproval of the PCU, contract and maintain throughout Project implementation pursuant to the Procurement Regulations and inaccordance with terms of reference satisfactory to the Association, one or more Independent Counter-Verification Agency (ICVA),with experience and qualifications in the health and social sectors acceptable to the Association, to conduct independentthird-party counter-verifications, in compliance with the verification protocols included in the PIM.

Schedule 2-I.D.(c) (i) for purposes of counter verification of the payments for the Eligible Expenditures for the PBCs under Part1.3 of the Project, the Ministry of Health, Public Hygiene and Universal Access to Care:(i) No later than six (6) months after theEffective Date, and with the approval of the PCU, contract and maintain throughout Project implementation pursuant to theProcurement Regulations and in accordance with terms of reference satisfactory to the Association, one or more IndependentCounter-Verification Agency (ICVA), with experience and qualifications in the health and social sectors acceptable to theAssociation, to conduct independent third-party counter-verifications, in compliance with the verification protocols included inthe PIM.

Schedule 2-IV. No later than six (6) months after the Effective Date, the Recipient shall provide evidence to the Association,acceptable to the Association of: (a) the issuance and approval of a Presidential Decree creating the integrated national healthinsurance entity, “Togo Social Insurance Agency (“TSHIA”), which shall absorb the existing entities such as Institut Nationald’Assurance Maladie (“INAM”); and (b) the establishment of a PIU within the TSHIA, in a manner acceptable to the Association.
